title: Admin Quickflow Autotuner and Safe-execute Policy
creator: Nina Park
description:
Problem: Support engineers frequently create ad-hoc admin quickflows (short playbooks) for first-response remediation. Differences in input shapes, batching, and permission guards cause variability in latency and safety. We want an "autotuner" that observes execution characteristics and synthesizes conservative default tuning (concurrency, batch windows, dry-run gating) plus a policy layer that enforces least-privilege execution for quickflows.

Goal: Build a lightweight autotuner service + policy shim that can: 1) collect execution telemetry for quickflows, 2) recommend tuned defaults per quickflow (concurrency, retry/backoff, idempotency hints), 3) provide a pre-execution dry-run simulation route for unsafe flows, and 4) apply a permissioned safe-execute policy (RBAC + scope checks) before running production steps. The feature should integrate with the Runbook-as-Tasks runtime and the Admin Console.

Scope: MVP focuses on quickflows invoked via the Admin Console and ops CLI. Does NOT include full autoloading of third-party scripts or heavy simulation of external side-effects (that will be phase 2).
acceptance_criteria: Autotuner collects per-quickflow metrics (avg duration, error rate, token/bandwidth usage) into ops telemetry pipeline
MVP recommendations API returns concurrency and batch/window defaults for a quickflow id
Safe-execute policy rejects flows that require scope escalation and surfaces a one-click escalation workflow
Dry-run endpoint performs a no-side-effect validation and returns a simulated result with confidence score
Integrates with Console: quickflow card shows recommended defaults and a toggle for dry-run before run
design_decisions: Use a thin service that stores aggregated metrics in ClickHouse (existing ops metrics cluster) rather than per-request stateful DB
Recommendation logic will start rule-based (heuristics + percentile thresholds) to avoid an initial ML maintenance burden; ML model is planned for phase 3
Dry-run will use a sandboxed validation layer that replays input through parser/validators and a mocked step runner; no external side-effects are performed
Permission policy leverages existing RBAC + scoped tokens; where missing, surface manual escalation to SRE on-call instead of auto-granting
tradeoffs_and_risks: Rule-based recommendations can be conservative and underutilize capacity initially — acceptable tradeoff for safety
Dry-run coverage is limited; some side-effecting steps cannot be fully simulated and will be flagged as 'requires staging verification'
Telemetry volume may increase; we will sample at 10% for high-frequency quickflows until storage/enrichment pipeline capacity is verified
Policy enforcement could add ~5-20ms overhead to each quickflow invocation; measured and acceptable versus safety gain
implementation_plan: Week 1: Instrument runbook runtime to emit compact execution events (quickflow_id, step_count, duration_ms, error_flag)
Week 2: Build aggregator job to rollup metrics into ClickHouse and expose a recommendations HTTP API
Week 3: Implement dry-run sandbox endpoint and integrate with Console quickflow card UI (feature flag behind ops.experimental.autotuner)
Week 4: Policy shim to call RBAC service and gating logic; end-to-end tests and canary rollout to internal SRE team
Post-MVP: Expand sampling, tune heuristics, and add a periodic job that re-evaluates recommendations
